title: The American West: History, Myth, and Legacy
description:
S01 E04 — Discoveries of Lewis and Clark
The journey of the two explorers who map the Louisiana Purchase between 1804 and 1806; how Lewis and Clark fit into the tradition of explorers looking for a water route to the Pacific; the political and geographic history of the Louisiana Purchase.

title: The Great Tours: Civil War Battlefields
description:
S01 E01 — The Power of Place: The Civil War in Context
Exploring the significance of battlefields and the methods employed by soldiers in combat.

title: The Great Tours: Civil War Battlefields
description:
S01 E02 — Manassas: The First Battle of Bull Run
Marching from Washington, Irvin McDowell's Union forces encounter P. G. T. Beauregard's Confederate troops at Virginia's Bull Run.

title: The Great Tours: Civil War Battlefields
description:
S01 E03 — The Seven Days' Battles
Robert E. Lee's Army of Northern Virginia and George B. McClellan's Army of the Potomac write a blood-soaked chapter in American history and alter the trajectory of the Civil War.

title: The Great Tours: Civil War Battlefields
description:
S01 E04 — A Return to Manassas: The Second Battle of Bull Run
In the Second Battle of Bull Run, lieutenants James Longstreet and Thomas Stonewall Jackson play a crucial role in securing victory for Robert E. Lee.

title: The Age of Benjamin Franklin
description:
S01 E01 — Benjamin Franklin and the American Dream
In Franklin's unfinished autobiography, he creates a persona for himself as a role model others may follow; there is more to Franklin than he shows on the page; surveying the book offers some foundational insights into his life and his worldview.

title: The Age of Benjamin Franklin
description:
S01 E02 — Meet the Franklins
The Franklins are a typical 18th-century family, extended across space; filled with comedy and tragedy, wealth and poverty; meeting his parents and siblings; learning the story of his wife and firstborn son; accompanying Franklin on his travels.

title: The Age of Benjamin Franklin
description:
S01 E03 — Benjamin Franklin's Boston Beginnings
One may associate Franklin with Philadelphia, but his roots lie in Boston; many of the virtues Franklin cultivates throughout his life grow from the values of the Boston Puritans; witnessing the events that Franklin experiences in his youth.

title: The Age of Benjamin Franklin
description:
S01 E04 — Benjamin Franklin and Philadelphia
Shifting attention to the City of Brotherly Love; 18th-century Philadelphia is one of the leading cities in British America; it is one of the leading cities in the British Empire; what makes this city so important; how the city shapes Franklin.

title: The Agency: A History of the CIA
description:
S01 E01 — Secrecy, Democracy, and the Birth of the CIA
Why the United States created a secret foreign intelligence service; examining three periods of U.S. government intelligence before the birth of the CIA; the American Revolution to the late 1930s; World War II; the postwar years from 1945 to 1947.

title: The Agency: A History of the CIA
description:
S01 E02 — George Kennan and the Rise of Covert Ops
How the CIA transformed from an intelligence agency to housing the United States' premier covert-action unit in the space of just two years; the role of George F. Kennan, who declared political warfare against the Soviet Union.

title: The Agency: A History of the CIA
description:
S01 E03 — The CIA, China, and the Korean War
The CIA's attention to Asia; how the CIA failed to rein in its emphasis on covert operations and restore its focus on intelligence; a lack of public scrutiny of the CIA's actions; the arrival of future CIA director Allen Dulles.

title: The Agency: A History of the CIA
description:
S01 E04 — The Iran Coup of August 1953
The 1953 Iran Coup and how it created a culture of covert action that would shape the CIA's future; studying the shifting political attitudes toward Iranian nationalism; analyzing the Iran operation; pondering who was most responsible.

title: The American West: History, Myth, and Legacy
description:
S01 E01 — Westward the Course of Empire
Some of the ways people think about the American West; how this vast, fascinating region comes into being; how it is shaped by centuries of myth-making; what about westward expansion fascinates every generation of Americans.

title: The American West: History, Myth, and Legacy
description:
S01 E02 — The West in the Colonial Era
Understanding the mark left on the American West by its earliest colonists; the Spaniards, who introduce horses; the French, who develop a complex trade system; the English, who have little interest in colonizing the west of the Appalachians.

title: The American West: History, Myth, and Legacy
description:
S01 E03 — Venturing Beyond the Appalachians
After the Revolutionary War, the land between the Appalachians and the Mississippi becomes part of the new republic; how the territory is organized; the Northwest Ordinance of 1787 creates a new set of rules that clashes with old realities.

title: The American West: History, Myth, and Legacy
description:
S01 E04 — Discoveries of Lewis and Clark
The journey of the two explorers who map the Louisiana Purchase between 1804 and 1806; how Lewis and Clark fit into the tradition of explorers looking for a water route to the Pacific; the political and geographic history of the Louisiana Purchase.

description:

S01 E02 — Manassas: The First Battle of Bull Run

title: The Great Tours: Civil War Battlefields
description:
S01 E04 — A Return to Manassas: The Second Battle of Bull Run
In the Second Battle of Bull Run, lieutenants James Longstreet and Thomas Stonewall Jackson play a crucial role in securing victory for Robert E. Lee.

title: World War II: Up Close and Personal
description:
S01 E01 — Hitler and the Nazi Youth
The horrors of Nazi Germany are one hallmark of World War II; pondering how ordinary German citizens find themselves participating in such heinous events; going inside the propaganda machine of Hitler's Germany; seeing how it targets the youth.

title: World War II: Up Close and Personal
description:
S01 E02 — Japanese Soldiers in Nanjing
The origins of World War II lie in Asia in 1931; tracing the invasion of 1937 and the Rape of Nanjing; witnessing the events through the eyes of a Chinese soldier and a Japanese journalist, young men who bear witness to the flesh and blood of battle.

title: World War II: Up Close and Personal
description:
S01 E03 — Panzer Leaders Who Changed Warfare
In addition to the story of people, World War II is the story of technology; perhaps nowhere is this more apparent than the tanks Germany uses to barrel across Poland and France in "lightning warfare"; how new technology defeats the old ways of war.

title: World War II: Up Close and Personal
description:
S01 E04 — Jews Inside the Warsaw Ghetto
Wartime Warsaw offers a gateway to the darkest events of the war; bearing witness as the city's Jews are rounded up and put in the ghetto, where the specter of disease and starvation always looms; stories from several of the ghetto's inhabitants.

title: Masters of War: History's Greatest Strategic Thinkers
description:
S01 E01 — Why Strategy Matters
If war is a gamble, then a strategy is key to success; a survey of why strategy is important; looking at World War II's "Operation Torch" as a case study for how the military should be used as an instrument of policy.

title: Masters of War: History's Greatest Strategic Thinkers
description:
S01 E02 — Thucydides On Strategy
A systematic look at what makes Thucydides perhaps history's first great strategist; his analysis of the Peloponnesian War; the political origins of the war; the Spartan and Athenian leadership; the social and moral implications of war.

title: Masters of War: History's Greatest Strategic Thinkers
description:
S01 E03 — Thucydides as a Possession for All Time
Joining a debate over the efficacy of the Sicilian Expedition; turning to the Melian Dialogue; the debate between realists and neoconservatives over the conduct of war; considering how this debate still plays out in contemporary America.

title: Masters of War: History's Greatest Strategic Thinkers
description:
S01 E04 — Sun Tzu's the Art of War
Sun Tzu's writing is popular in the modern world; the historical context for "Master Sun's Military Methods"; an overview of Sun Tzu's strategy for war, which is to be efficient, avoid protracted wars and value the commander's intellect and skill.

title: Masters of War: History's Greatest Strategic Thinkers
description:
S01 E05 — Sun Tzu Through Time
Charting Sun Tzu's historical importance throughout Chinese history, in feudal and modern Japan, and in the modern West; learning Sun Tzu's strategy of deception in action by exploring Operation Fortitude in the Allied invasion of Normandy.

title: Masters of War: History's Greatest Strategic Thinkers
description:
S01 E06 — Machiavelli's the Art of War
Learning about Machiavelli, the Italian Renaissance man who writes his own "The Art of War" in which he advocates a citizen-army; going through Machiavelli's book of tactics, which is his recommendation for Florentine military rulers.

title: Masters of War: History's Greatest Strategic Thinkers
description:
S01 E07 — Machiavelli's Discourses On Livy
Discovering fortuna, which is Machiavelli's philosophy of circumstances, and virtu, which is his recipe for military action; the strategies Machiavelli thinks a republican military should adopt; the qualities to look for in a good commander.

title: Masters of War: History's Greatest Strategic Thinkers
description:
S01 E08 — The Napoleonic Revolution in War
Experiencing the battles of Jena and Auerstedt during the Napoleonic Wars; these two decisive victories demonstrate the radical transformation of warfare; they give rise to Antoine-Henri Jomini and Carl von Clausewitz, two important masters of war.

title: War in the Modern World
description:
S01 E01 — Afghanistan and the Nature of Modern War
In the course's inaugural episode, begin to explore the transformation of violent conflicts between major world powers by delving into a particularly recent example: America's 20-year war in Afghanistan.

title: War in the Modern World
description:
S01 E02 — Nightmare Scenarios of Modern War
The factors that explain why wars between great powers look different nowadays, and explore what future conflicts could look like between the United States and two of its major adversaries.

title: War in the Modern World
description:
S01 E03 — The Tools of Modern Warfare
How five contemporary technologies-the Kalashnikov assault rifle, improvised explosive devices, guided missiles, drones, and cyber warfare-redefined the rules of battle and leveled the playing field between world powers and insurgent groups.

title: War in the Modern World
description:
S01 E04 — From World War to Cold War
The series of events that followed World War II from the allied occupation of Germany to the Greek Civil War; how the Soviet Union contended with insurgencies and the beginnings of conflict between the United States and the USSR.

title: Great Board Games of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E01 — Bearing Off: The Story of Backgammon
During the Third Crusade, the European soldiers spend the winter playing the ancient game of Tables, which would evolve into backgammon by the 20th century.

title: Great Board Games of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E02 — Senet: Egypt's Game of the Afterlife
Unearthed artifacts from King Tutankhamun's tomb include Senet boards. Historians study the hieroglyphs and investigate the abrupt disappearance of this ancient Egyptian game.

title: Great Board Games of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E03 — Chess: The Evolution of a Strategy Icon
Developed during the Guptas' rule in India, Chaturanga is a strategy game resembling chess. It gradually wended its way westward to become what it is in the present.

title: Great Board Games of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E04 — Chess's Eastern Cousins: Shogi and Xiangqi
The East Asian games of Xiangqi and Shogi are potentially connected to Chaturanga and chess, but a lack of documentation makes it difficult to ascertain anything.

title: Great Board Games of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E05 — Go: A Game of Near-Infinite Complexity
Go is an intricate strategy game that outshines chess in East Asia because of its challenging nature and unique setup.

title: Great Board Games of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E06 — Sowing Seeds: Africa's Mancala Family
Mancala is a family of traditional African games dating back over 7,000 years. Awari and Bao are two members that fall on opposite ends of the spectrum of difficulty.

title: Decoding the Secrets of Egyptian Hieroglyphs
description:
S01 E01 — Why Egypt Needed Hieroglyphs
Understanding why Ancient Egypt has to invent some form of writing; central to this introduction is a study of the Narmer Palette; its writing sets standards and conventions that would be followed for 3,000 years.

title: Decoding the Secrets of Egyptian Hieroglyphs
description:
S01 E02 — The Ancient Egyptian Alphabet
Learning the hieroglyphic alphabet; how to write and position each hieroglyph, including a stylized hand, a horned viper and two hieroglyphs for which English does not have a letter; transcribing one's name from English to ancient Egyptian.

title: Decoding the Secrets of Egyptian Hieroglyphs
description:
S01 E03 — How a Language Becomes Lost
Wondering how it is possible for a language used by the world's greatest civilization to become lost; charting the rise and fall of Ancient Egypt's kingdoms; investigating the ways Christianity replaces hieroglyphs with Greek letters.

title: Decoding the Secrets of Egyptian Hieroglyphs
description:
S01 E04 — Napoleon in Egypt
Exploring how hieroglyphs and the ability to read them are rediscovered during Napoleon's invasion of Egypt; considering the birth of Egyptology; the role of ushabtis, statues of servants that are buried with prominent Egyptians.

title: World Heritage Sites: Exploring the World's Greatest Places
description:
S01 E01 — Paleolithic Cave Art of Spain and France
The oldest paintings in the world, in the extraordinary cave art of Altamira, Lascaux, and Chauvet.

title: World Heritage Sites: Exploring the World's Greatest Places
description:
S01 E02 — The Taj Mahal of Agra
Learning about the builder of Taj, the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan, and his beloved wife Mumtaz Mahal, for whom it was built.

title: World Heritage Sites: Exploring the World's Greatest Places
description:
S01 E03 — Australia's Great Barrier Reef
The Great Barrier Reef is one of the world's natural wonders, drawing travelers to its shimmering, multicolored coral reefs, teeming with fascinating marine life.

title: World Heritage Sites: Exploring the World's Greatest Places
description:
S01 E04 — The Mogao Grottoes and Manuscripts
The Mogao Grottoes, dug out of cliffs in the desert of northwestern China, contain one of the most dazzling collections of Buddhist art in the world.

title: World Heritage Sites: Exploring the World's Greatest Places
description:
S01 E05 — Persepolis, the Great Persian Capital
The citadel of Persepolis was the capital of the Achaemenid Empire for nearly 200 years.

title: World Heritage Sites: Exploring the World's Greatest Places
description:
S01 E06 — Easter Island and the Moai
The moai, the colossal statues of Easter Island, are a testament to human innovation.

title: Herodotus: The Father of History
description:
S01 E01 — Herodotus and History
Identifying key issues of definition and terminology; explaining what is known about the life of Herodotus; background on the ancient Greek world; summarizing the momentous events, particularly the Persian Wars, that spur Herodotus to write.

title: Herodotus: The Father of History
description:
S01 E02 — \"Inquiry\" and the Birth of History
Herodotus is not the first Greek to write about the past; knowing makes him original; how he explains, in the very first sentence of his work and one that richly rewards close reading, the what, why and how of his monumental effort.

title: Herodotus: The Father of History
description:
S01 E03 — Myth, Legend, and Oral Tradition
Knowing how Herodotus deals with the vast and complicated body of traditional narratives that inform the Greek world; how his subject and his angle on it both resemble and differ from older accounts of the ways and causes of things.

title: Herodotus: The Father of History
description:
S01 E04 — Homeric Epic and the East-West Conflict
For all ancient Greeks, Homer is a pervasive influence; Herodotus models his work on the "Iliad" and the "Odyssey," yet he departs from the Homeric and gives the uniquely Herodotean perspective.

title: The Darwinian Revolution
description:
S01 E01 — The Meaning of Evolution
Pondering why Darwin is so revolutionary; his breakthrough is not in introducing the idea of evolution, which has long been debated, but in proposing how evolution occurs; surveying these and other themes that are developed in the course.

title: The Darwinian Revolution
description:
S01 E02 — The Way It Used to Be
Examining the traditional worldview in the West, which is based on the biblical account of creation fixed at 4004 B.C.; an allied idea is the Great Chain of Being, pictured as an immutable scale of life forms from the most primitive to God himself.

title: The Darwinian Revolution
description:
S01 E03 — Theories of Evolution in the 18th Century
Studying three 18th-century thinkers; Benoit de Maillet, who estimates the age of the cosmos; Georges Buffon, who believes living things descend from more primal forms; Pierre Simon Laplace, who proposes a theory for the solar system's formation.

title: The Darwinian Revolution
description:
S01 E04 — Fossils and Catastrophism
At the end of the 18th century, fossils are not necessarily regarded as actual remains of living things; they become central to the work of Georges Cuvier, who connects them to extinct species which he believes died out in violent catastrophes.

title: Books That Matter: The Analects of Confucius
description:
S01 E01 — The Hidden Teaching Dynamic of the Analects
Getting a broader view of Confucius and his style of teaching; examining how the text's performative nature holds its diverse teachings together; exploring Confucius's mission to return China to a more harmonious era in its history.

title: Books That Matter: The Analects of Confucius
description:
S01 E02 — The Analects: A Bird's-Eye View
The "Analects" should not just be read, but lived; how to enter the book's world by considering Confucius's imaginative ideas about living in society; practicing one's ability to navigate through the book's tangle of information and questions.

title: Books That Matter: The Analects of Confucius
description:
S01 E03 — The Man We Call Confucius
Who Confucius is; how he manages to become one of the most important figures in world history; what historians know about Confucius; the opinions of thinkers like Mencius and Xunzi; several illuminating passages from Chapter 10 of the "Analects".

title: Books That Matter: The Analects of Confucius
description:
S01 E04 — How the Analects Is Organized
The structure of the "Analects" offers a helpful way to understand the text's deeper meanings: breaking down Confucius's book into its chapters, the scattered nature of its tiny nuggets of knowledge, and the generations of historical commentary.

title: Introduction to Paleontology
description:
S01 E01 — History on a Geological Scale
Taking a virtual walk from the Washington Monument to the U.S. Capitol to explore the 4.54 billion-year history of Earth, with each stride representing 1 to 2 million years; along the way, fossils paint a picture of life on Earth from its start.

title: Introduction to Paleontology
description:
S01 E02 — Life Cast in Ancient Stone
Learning about those whose curiosity about the Earth and its fossils leads to the development of the science of paleontology; studying the geographic, climatic and chemical requirements for a living organism to leave behind its fossilized record.

title: Introduction to Paleontology
description:
S01 E03 — Tools of the Paleontological Trade
In addition to the basic mechanical tools still used in the field today, paleontologists have an exciting digital tool chest; dispersive x-ray spectroscopy and x-ray computer tomography and their use to examine fossils of varying sizes and shapes.

title: Introduction to Paleontology
description:
S01 E04 — How Do You Fossilize Behavior?
While the fossilized remains of some organisms are rarely found, the evidence of their existence, as they interacted with the environment, exists; learning how trace fossils help understand the early evolution of the biosphere and animal life.

title: Herodotus: The Father of History
description:
S01 E01 — Herodotus and History
Identifying key issues of definition and terminology; explaining what is known about the life of Herodotus; background on the ancient Greek world; summarizing the momentous events, particularly the Persian Wars, that spur Herodotus to write.

title: Herodotus: The Father of History
description:
S01 E02 — \"Inquiry\" and the Birth of History
Herodotus is not the first Greek to write about the past; knowing makes him original; how he explains, in the very first sentence of his work and one that richly rewards close reading, the what, why and how of his monumental effort.

title: Herodotus: The Father of History
description:
S01 E03 — Myth, Legend, and Oral Tradition
Knowing how Herodotus deals with the vast and complicated body of traditional narratives that inform the Greek world; how his subject and his angle on it both resemble and differ from older accounts of the ways and causes of things.

title: Herodotus: The Father of History
description:
S01 E04 — Homeric Epic and the East-West Conflict
For all ancient Greeks, Homer is a pervasive influence; Herodotus models his work on the "Iliad" and the "Odyssey," yet he departs from the Homeric and gives the uniquely Herodotean perspective.

title: The Darwinian Revolution
description:
S01 E01 — The Meaning of Evolution
Pondering why Darwin is so revolutionary; his breakthrough is not in introducing the idea of evolution, which has long been debated, but in proposing how evolution occurs; surveying these and other themes that are developed in the course.

title: The Darwinian Revolution
description:
S01 E02 — The Way It Used to Be
Examining the traditional worldview in the West, which is based on the biblical account of creation fixed at 4004 B.C.; an allied idea is the Great Chain of Being, pictured as an immutable scale of life forms from the most primitive to God himself.

title: The Darwinian Revolution
description:
S01 E03 — Theories of Evolution in the 18th Century
Studying three 18th-century thinkers; Benoit de Maillet, who estimates the age of the cosmos; Georges Buffon, who believes living things descend from more primal forms; Pierre Simon Laplace, who proposes a theory for the solar system's formation.

title: The Darwinian Revolution
description:

At the end of the 18th century, fossils are not necessarily regarded as actual remains of living things; they become central to the work of Georges Cuvier, who connects them to extinct species which he believes died out in violent catastrophes.

title: History's Great Military Blunders and the Lessons They Teach
description:
S01 E01 — Petersburg: Union Digs Its Own Grave - 1864
Following the chain of events that led to the Civil War's ill-fated Battle of the Crater; what can happen in warfare when a plan goes awry due to various factors; the phenomenon of military blunders and what they can teach people.

title: History's Great Military Blunders and the Lessons They Teach
description:
S01 E02 — Syracuse: Athens's Second Front - 413 B.C.
From initiating a second front with a new enemy to dividing supreme command among multiple generals; how failures of decision-making and leadership spelled disaster for the Greek city state of Athens in the outcome of the Peloponnesian War.

title: The Persian Empire
description:
S01 E01 — Rethinking the Persian Empire
Cyrus, Darius and Xerxes; these Persian kings are sometimes stereotyped as one-dimensional despots in Greek histories; the truth about the Achaemenid Persian Empire; an empire that stretches from Egypt and Asia Minor, all the way to the Indus Valley.

title: The Persian Empire
description:
S01 E02 — Questioning the Sources
Greek historians provide valuable information about the Persian Empire; the Greek perspective is often negatively biased; archaeology uncovers inscriptions, administrative tablets and other documents that let the Persians speak for themselves.

title: Understanding Russia: A Cultural History
description:
S01 E01 — A Russian Past, the Putin Future
The heart of Russian history and culture; examining many themes; the enormity of Russia's geography; its desire for power; its search for an organic cultural identity; exploring the beginnings of Russia in the land known as Rus'.

title: Understanding Russia: A Cultural History
description:
S01 E02 — Ivan the Terrible's 500-Year Reign
Ivan the Terrible's reign is a cultural and historical symbol of Russian leadership; how he uses cultural symbols to create a spectacle of autocracy; knowing to what extent he sets the standard for subsequent centuries of the Russian leadership.

title: Herodotus: The Father of History
description:
S01 E01 — Herodotus and History
Identifying key issues of definition and terminology; explaining what is known about the life of Herodotus; background on the ancient Greek world; summarizing the momentous events, particularly the Persian Wars, that spur Herodotus to write.

title: Herodotus: The Father of History
description:
S01 E02 — \"Inquiry\" and the Birth of History
Herodotus is not the first Greek to write about the past; knowing makes him original; how he explains, in the very first sentence of his work and one that richly rewards close reading, the what, why and how of his monumental effort.

title: Great Board Games of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E01 — Bearing Off: The Story of Backgammon
During the Third Crusade, the European soldiers spend the winter playing the ancient game of Tables, which would evolve into backgammon by the 20th century.

title: Great Board Games of the Ancient World
description:
S01 E02 — Senet: Egypt's Game of the Afterlife
Unearthed artifacts from King Tutankhamun's tomb include Senet boards. Historians study the hieroglyphs and investigate the abrupt disappearance of this ancient Egyptian game.

title: Decoding the Secrets of Egyptian Hieroglyphs
description:
S01 E01 — Why Egypt Needed Hieroglyphs
Understanding why Ancient Egypt has to invent some form of writing; central to this introduction is a study of the Narmer Palette; its writing sets standards and conventions that would be followed for 3,000 years.

title: Decoding the Secrets of Egyptian Hieroglyphs
description:
S01 E02 — The Ancient Egyptian Alphabet
Learning the hieroglyphic alphabet; how to write and position each hieroglyph, including a stylized hand, a horned viper and two hieroglyphs for which English does not have a letter; transcribing one's name from English to ancient Egyptian.

title: World Heritage Sites: Exploring the World's Greatest Places
description:
S01 E01 — Paleolithic Cave Art of Spain and France
The oldest paintings in the world, in the extraordinary cave art of Altamira, Lascaux, and Chauvet.

title: World Heritage Sites: Exploring the World's Greatest Places
description:
S01 E02 — The Taj Mahal of Agra
Learning about the builder of Taj, the Mughal emperor Shah Jahan, and his beloved wife Mumtaz Mahal, for whom it was built.

title: Masters of War: History's Greatest Strategic Thinkers
description:
S01 E01 — Why Strategy Matters
If war is a gamble, then a strategy is key to success; a survey of why strategy is important; looking at World War II's "Operation Torch" as a case study for how the military should be used as an instrument of policy.

title: Masters of War: History's Greatest Strategic Thinkers
description:
S01 E02 — Thucydides On Strategy
A systematic look at what makes Thucydides perhaps history's first great strategist; his analysis of the Peloponnesian War; the political origins of the war; the Spartan and Athenian leadership; the social and moral implications of war.
